blocks.text: MATH 120: Statistics for the Life Sciences
Department of Mathematics
Course Information
This course introduces statistical thinking for students in biology, health and environmental science. Lectures meet Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 9:00 a.m. in Science Hall 104. 1
Prerequisites
Precalculus or equivalent placement score
Basic familiarity with spreadsheets
What You Will Learn
Summarize data with tables, graphs and numerical measures.
Use probability to describe chance variation.
Estimate population quantities with confidence intervals.
Test claims with hypothesis tests and interpret p-values carefully.
Assessment
Component Weight Notes Weekly quizzes 20% Lowest two dropped Homework 20% Weekly, submitted online Midterm exams 30% Two exams, 15% each Final exam 30% Cumulative
Lecture recordings are posted within 24 hours of each class.
Policies
Attendance
Attendance is expected but not graded. Quizzes cannot be made up, which is why the lowest two scores are dropped.
Academic Integrity
You may discuss homework with classmates. You must write your own solutions and list the names of anyone you worked with at the top of each submission.
Accessibility
If you use accommodations, send your letter to the instructor in the first week. Course materials can be provided in alternative formats on request.
Textbook
Required: Introductory Statistics (OpenStax), available free online. Chapters 1 through 10 are covered.
